newsitem.title: UK: Tight UK security hits off-line air cargo exports.
newsitem.headline: Tight UK security hits off-line air cargo exports.

text.p: Britain's tight air cargo security regulations are acting as a disadvantage to carriers wanting to use London Heathrow for shipments originating outside the UK, Air Canada's head of cargo in Europe said.

The need for many containers and pallets to go through the single decompression chamber at Heathrow has resulted in cargo from some 'off-line' markets missing flights, having been delayed in queues to use the machine, Air Canada's Des Vertannes told Reuters in an interview.

Air Canada uses flights from Heathrow for cargo trucked from Belgium, the Netherlands and Ireland and Vertannes said these consignments would not face the same regulations if airfreighted from Frankfurt or Paris.
As well as Heathrow, Air Canada flies to Canada from Frankfurt, Paris and Zurich.

"What we would hope for is a level playing field (in the EU) on Department of Transport (DoT) security requirements," said Vertannes, who is Air Canada's general manager cargo for Europe, Africa and the Middle East.

"At the moment, we are effectively penalised for bringing cargo through London as the UK security requirements are triggered when cargo coming from an (DOT) unlisted or 'unknown' shipper or forwarder is 'trucked over the water'," he added.
A loose cargo consignment can be x-rayed and then needs repacking, which is both time consuming and costly.
One solution would be to have unlisted off-market shippers and forwarders registered with the DoT and thereby converted to a higher security status. said Vertannes.
Another is for Heathrow to have more decompression facilities, he added.
European shippers and forwarders need to be persuaded that it is worth their while to become 'DoT-listed' and not just use continental European airports, and Air Canada is talking to them about this.

Two weeks ago the British International Freight Association (BIFA) said the UK's air cargo security regime was inadequate as some of the 'listed' cargo agents were not adequately screening their shipper customers, some of whom it said were not sticking to the security regulations.
These off-line markets are very important for Air Canada, which has added extra Sunday flights due to a lack of capacity on this peak day for air cargo traffic, Vertannes said.
Air Canada has tried to attract this business from Benelux and Ireland and has given the Belgian and Dutch cargo markets dedicated ex-Heathrow flights to Toronto.
Each Sunday since June 15, Air Canada has dedicated one Boeing 767-200 to Belgian and another 767-200 to Dutch cargo -- each have a cargo uplift of 12 to 15 tonnes.
Air Canada has a total of five London departures to Toronto each Sunday including one 747 Combi with an uplift of 40 tonnes.
